account: Phoebe Tesoriere, 23, from Cardiff, Wales, is a former special educational needs teacher. She had a limp since childhood. From 2022 she was diagnosed with epilepsy, then Todd's paralysis, and was repeatedly told that her symptoms were anxiety. In January 2025 she fell down stairs and spent months in hospital. In July 2025 a seizure left her in a coma (three days per BBC Wales, 48 hours per the SWNS report in WalesOnline). After discharge she entered her symptoms into ChatGPT. It returned a list of possible conditions including hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP). She took the suggestion to her general practitioner, who agreed that it was a “plausible reason”. Genetic testing confirmed HSP, in August 2025 according to WalesOnline, which also reports the complex quadriplegic type. There is no treatment. She uses a wheelchair, attends physiotherapy and is fundraising for a specialist chair. Cardiff and Vale University Health Board said that it was “sorry to hear about Phoebe's experience while in our care”. It would not comment on an individual case. The account rests on her own statements to SWNS (6 April 2026) and BBC Wales (10 April 2026). No clinical document is among the sources. BBC Wales reported on 5 October 2026 that Tesoriere, then 24 and a student at Cardiff Metropolitan University, has hereditary spastic paraplegia and uses a wheelchair. The same report says that she now lives in Bath; it does not mention ChatGPT.

The prompt, the model version and the full candidate list are not reported. Only news reports quoting the patient are among the sources. The health board declined to comment on the case.

fields.headline: ChatGPT suggests a rare condition that a genetic test confirms
fields.title: ChatGPT lists hereditary spastic paraplegia for Phoebe Tesoriere, 23, after four years of misdiagnosis; her GP agrees and genetic testing confirms it

fields.account: Phoebe Tesoriere, 23, from Cardiff, Wales, is a former special educational needs teacher. She had a limp since childhood. From 2022 she was diagnosed with epilepsy, then Todd's paralysis, and was repeatedly told that her symptoms were anxiety. In January 2025 she fell down stairs and spent months in hospital. In July 2025 a seizure left her in a coma (three days per BBC Wales, 48 hours per the SWNS report in WalesOnline). After discharge she entered her symptoms into ChatGPT. It returned a list of possible conditions including hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP). She took the suggestion to her general practitioner, who agreed that it was a “plausible reason”. Genetic testing confirmed HSP, in August 2025 according to WalesOnline, which also reports the complex quadriplegic type. There is no treatment. She uses a wheelchair, attends physiotherapy and is fundraising for a specialist chair. Cardiff and Vale University Health Board said that it was “sorry to hear about Phoebe's experience while in our care”. It would not comment on an individual case. The account rests on her own statements to SWNS (6 April 2026) and BBC Wales (10 April 2026). No clinical document is among the sources. BBC Wales reported on 5 October 2026 that Tesoriere, then 24 and a student at Cardiff Metropolitan University, has hereditary spastic paraplegia and uses a wheelchair. The same report says that she now lives in Bath; it does not mention ChatGPT.
